title: Content Depth Matters in Short-Video Recommendation: Rethinking the Attention Economy
abstract: arXiv:2608.13990v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Driven by the attention economy, short-video Recommender Systems (RSs) are primarily optimized to maximize user engagement by promoting videos that capture attention within seconds. These systems inherently favor shallow-content videos that are effective at attracting immediate attention. However, growing evidence suggests that prolonged exposure to such content may negatively affect users' cognitive engagement and mental well-being, raising concerns about the long-term societal impact of the short-video platform. To tackle this challenge, this paper introduces a new metric, the \textbf{Content Depth Score (CDS)}, to quantify the content depth of short videos. CDS measures the extent to which a video is expected to stimulate higher-order cognitive processes, using a seven-level scale grounded in established theories of cognitive psychology and learning. translated_title: 短视频推荐中内容深度的重要性：重新思考注意力经济
translated_abstract: arXiv:2608.13990v1 公告类型：新 摘要：受注意力经济驱动，短视频推荐系统（RSs）主要优化目标是通过推广能在几秒内吸引注意力的视频来最大化用户参与度。这些系统天然倾向于偏好能有效吸引即时注意力的浅层内容视频。然而，越来越多的证据表明，长期接触此类内容可能对用户的认知参与和心理健康产生负面影响，引发对短视频平台长期社会影响的担忧。为应对这一挑战，本文引入了一种新指标——\textbf{内容深度评分（CDS）}，用于量化短视频的内容深度。CDS基于认知心理学和学习领域的成熟理论，采用七级量表来衡量视频预期刺激高阶认知过程的程度。作为迈向这一愿景的初步步骤，我们提出了\textbf{SCOPE-Bench}，这是首个基准测试平台。
tldr: 本文提出内容深度评分（CDS）指标和SCOPE-Bench基准，以量化短视频内容深度，旨在缓解注意力经济下浅层内容对用户认知和心理健康的不良影响。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces the Content Depth Score (CDS) metric and SCOPE-Bench benchmark to quantify content depth in short videos, aiming to mitigate the negative cognitive and mental health impacts of shallow content under the attention economy.
